        ### Question
        Which of the following clinical scenarios is most likely to correspond to multiple sclerosis?

        ### Options
        opa. 36-year-old woman who notices electric shocks from the cervical region to the buttocks when bending the neck, with exploratory finding of pyramidalism in both legs and hemihypoestesia with level D1.
opb. A 22-year-old woman with generalized tonic-clonic seizures of recent onset, normal neurological examination and mesial temporal sclerosis in cranial MRI.
opc. A 42-year-old man with ascending subacute paresthesias on both legs and arms, symmetric paraparesis and universal areflexia.
opd. A 54-year-old man with cognitive deterioration of a rapidly progressive course in which cranial MRI showed multiple periventricular hyperintense lesions and subcortical lacunae.

### Reasoning Chains per Option:
CHAIN: "36-year-old woman" -> "electric shocks from cervical region to buttocks when bending neck" -> "Lhermitte's sign" -> "pyramidalism in both legs" -> "hemihypoesthesia with level D1" -> "demyelinating lesions in CNS" -> "multiple sclerosis" -> 95%
CHAIN: "22-year-old woman" -> "generalized tonic-clonic seizures" -> "normal neurological examination" -> "mesial temporal sclerosis in cranial MRI" -> "temporal lobe epilepsy" -> "not typical for multiple sclerosis" -> 20%
CHAIN: "42-year-old man" -> "ascending subacute paresthesias in legs and arms" -> "symmetric paraparesis" -> "universal areflexia" -> "Guillain-Barré syndrome" -> "not typical for multiple sclerosis" -> 15%
CHAIN: "54-year-old man" -> "cognitive deterioration" -> "rapidly progressive course" -> "multiple periventricular hyperintense lesions" -> "subcortical lacunae" -> "vascular dementia or other neurodegenerative disorder" -> "not typical for multiple sclerosis" -> 25%

### Retrieved Evidence Paths (broad but correct):
(Dementia, Vascular)-CAUSES->(Disease)-CAUSES->(Multiple Sclerosis)
(Hippocampal sclerosis)-CAUSES->(Epilepsy, Temporal Lobe)
(Epilepsy, Temporal Lobe)-CAUSES->(Disease)-CAUSES->(Multiple Sclerosis)
